input.reasoning:
Estimation approach: convert story points to engineering hours using a standard 1 point ≈ 6 hours baseline for a mid-level developer, then split effort across roles per task type (backend/frontend/QA/devops), and apply a role's proportional capacity (FTE) as a sanity check against elapsed calendar time. Total points = 5+8+8+13+8+5+13+21 = 81 points.

Task-level role split (hours), based on task nature:
- PW-1 CI pipeline & staging (5 pts, High): DevOps-heavy. ~30 pts-hours total -> DevOps 24h, Backend 6h.
- PW-2 Design system/component library (8 pts, Medium): Frontend-heavy. Frontend 40h, QA 8h.
- PW-3 Registration/login (8 pts, Urgent): Backend+Frontend+QA. Backend 32h, Frontend 16h, QA 8h.
- PW-4 RBAC (13 pts, High): Backend-heavy with UI enforcement. Backend 52h, Frontend 16h, QA 10h.
- PW-5 Customer dashboard (8 pts, High): Frontend-heavy with backend API. Backend 16h, Frontend 32h, QA 8h.
- PW-6 Invoice list/detail (5 pts, Medium): Backend 16h, Frontend 20h, QA 6h.
- PW-7 Payment integration (13 pts, Urgent): Backend-heavy, critical, QA heavy for reconciliation. Backend 60h, Frontend 8h, QA 16h, DevOps 4h (webhook infra).
- PW-8 Legacy data migration (21 pts, High): Backend + DevOps heavy, QA for validation. Backend 90h, DevOps 20h, QA 16h.

Sum per role:
Backend: 6+32+52+16+16+60+90 = 272h
Frontend: 40+16+16+32+20+8 = 132h
QA: 8+8+10+8+6+16+16 = 72h
DevOps: 24+4+20 = 48h

Check capacity proportionality: Backend 1.5 FTE ~ 60h/week/person *1.5=90h/week capacity; 272h/90 ≈ 3 weeks. Frontend 1.0 FTE ~ 40h/week; 132h ≈ 3.3 weeks. QA 0.6 FTE ~24h/week; 72h ≈ 3 weeks. DevOps 0.4 FTE ~16h/week; 48h ≈ 3 weeks. Roughly consistent ~3-3.5 week sprint-equivalent effort, reasonable for backlog convergence, though DevOps and QA are thin (0.4 and 0.6 FTE) and will be the pacing constraint for CI/QA-heavy tasks — flagged as assumption/risk.

Costs:
Backend: 272 * 98.33 = 26,753.76
Frontend: 132 * 90 = 11,880
QA: 72 * 70 = 5,040
DevOps: 48 * 110 = 5,280

Labour subtotal = 26,753.76+11,880+5,040+5,280 = 48,953.76

Non-labour costs: Stripe integration test/sandbox fees, cloud staging environment hosting, data migration tooling/licenses, contingency for legacy Oracle export tooling.
- Cloud staging environment & CI tooling (3 months): 1,200
- Stripe sandbox/test transaction fees & compliance review: 800
- Data migration tooling license (ETL/Oracle connector) one-time: 2,500
- Contingency buffer (10% of labour) for unknowns given no historical actuals: 4,895

Non-labour subtotal = 1,200+800+2,500+4,895 = 9,395

Total base estimate = 48,953.76 + 9,395 = 58,348.76

Priority breakdown (sum points cost proportionally by priority using labour+non-labour split roughly by point-weighted share):
Total points 81. 
Urgent points = PW-3(8)+PW-7(13)=21 -> 21/81=25.9%
High points = PW-1(5)+PW-4(13)+PW-5(8)+PW-8(21)=47 -> 47/81=58.0%
Medium points = PW-2(8)+PW-6(5)=13 -> 13/81=16.0%

Apply to total 58,348.76:
Urgent: 25.9%*58,348.76 ≈ 15,112
High: 58.0%*58,348.76 ≈ 33,842
Medium: 16.0%*58,348.76 ≈ 9,335 (rounding adjustments to sum to total)

Scenarios:
- Best case (P50, optimistic execution, no rework): ~ -8% => 53,681
- Most likely (P50 baseline as estimated): 58,349
- Worst case (P90, migration/integration complications, QA/DevOps bottleneck causing overtime or contractor top-up): +25% => 72,936

Reductions/recommendations:
1. Defer PW-2 (Design system) to a later phase since it's Medium priority and not blocking urgent features — saves its full allocated cost (Frontend 40h + QA 8h = 40*90+8*70=3600+560=4160).
2. Reduce QA scope on PW-6 (Invoice list) by combining manual QA with automated regression reuse from PW-3, saving ~4 hours QA (~$280) — low-confidence marginal saving; better to cut non-labour contingency instead.
3. Trim contingency buffer from 10% to 6% once a pilot sprint establishes real velocity data, saving ~$1,958.
4. Use managed Stripe-hosted checkout instead of fully custom webhook/reconciliation UI to cut Backend hours on PW-7 by ~15h (~$1,475).
5. Negotiate a fixed-fee data migration tooling license via vendor discount or open-source ETL instead of commercial connector, saving ~$1,500 non-labour.

I'll list top 3-4 concrete reductions with savings and effect/confidence.
</reasoning>

nonLabourLines.description: Cloud staging environment & CI tooling (approx. 3 months)
Stripe sandbox/test transaction fees & PCI compliance review
Data migration tooling / Oracle ETL connector license (one-time)
Contingency buffer (~10% of labour) given no historical actuals

assumptions: No historical actuals (real spend data) exist for this project yet; estimate is based on story-point-to-hour heuristics (1 point ≈ 6 engineering hours) and role-mix judgment per task type, not observed velocity.

Story points converted to hours and split across roles based on typical effort profile for each task (e.g., CI/staging is DevOps-heavy, dashboard/design work is Frontend-heavy, migration/payments are Backend+QA heavy).

QA Engineer (0.6 FTE) and DevOps Engineer (0.4 FTE) are thinly staffed relative to backlog demand; their allocated hours (72h and 48h respectively) will likely be the pacing constraint and may extend calendar duration even though cost is capped by hours worked.
Backend Developer capacity (1.5 FTE) comfortably covers the 272 allocated hours over the estimated delivery window (~3-3.5 weeks of overlapping work).
Legacy data migration (PW-8) assumes a semi-automated ETL approach; fully manual reconciliation of 2M invoice lines would significantly increase Backend and QA hours.
Payment integration (PW-7) assumes use of Stripe's standard hosted APIs/webhooks rather than a fully custom PCI-scope solution.
A 10% labour contingency is included in non-labour costs to cover estimation uncertainty given the lack of historical actuals; this should be revisited once real velocity data is available.
Priority-based cost breakdown is apportioned by story-point weight per priority tier as a reasonable proxy, since tasks are not individually costed by priority.

reductions.effect: Removes 40 Frontend hours and 8 QA hours from current phase scope; component library work is rescheduled to a subsequent release.

reductions.effect: Cuts ~15 Backend Developer hours by leveraging Stripe's pre-built, PCI-compliant components instead of custom-building equivalent flows.

reductions.description: Replace commercial Oracle ETL connector license with an open-source or in-house scripted migration approach for PW-8.
reductions.effect: Removes the one-time data migration tooling license non-labour cost; adds some Backend scripting time already accounted for in current hour estimate.
